paper_title: Anisotropic cosmic optical background bound for decaying dark matter in light of the LORRI anomaly
notes: Headline curve is the 'HST 0.606um (this work)' exclusion in Fig. 3 (ALP2-crop.pdf in the e-print), the ALP-photon coupling plane for ALP dominant DM (R=1, q_gamma=2). Extracted by vector-drawing recovery of the purple filled region's lower boundary; axis calibration from tick labels (x: m=5..30 eV linear; y: log g, 1e-12 at y=381.25px, 136.15 px/decade). The paper's g_chi_gamma_gamma equals the canonical g_agamma exactly: Eq.(3) gives Gamma = g^2 m^3/(64*pi), the standard a->2gamma decay rate for L=-(g/4) a F Ftilde, so no conversion is applied. The 'HST 0.85um (this work)' region (blue) is a second, weaker bound (g ~ 3.5e-11 at m=10 eV, min mass ~4 eV) shown in the same figure; the 0.606um curve is more stringent everywhere and matches the LORRI-anomaly wavelength, so it is reported as the main result. Bound is a new limit derived by this paper from HST COB anisotropy data (Ref. 45) via a chi^2 test; 95% CL. Left edge at m=5 eV is a genuine applicability cutoff; right edge at 30 eV is the plot boundary. Excluded region lies above the reported curve. dm_density set null: this is a cosmological decaying-DM / EBL-anisotropy bound depending on the mean DM density (Planck), not a local halo density.
